note: Real-world SQL harvested from open-source FiveM resources that depend on oxmysql. `normalised: true` means a Lua interpolation/concatenation/string.format that could not be statically resolved was replaced with a concrete value (a `?` placeholder, a resolved table/column name, or a representative expansion of a loop-built clause). Everything else is verbatim. Oversized data-seed INSERTs in esx_core's legacy.sql (items, job_grades, vehicles, fine_types) were deliberately skipped rather than truncated, since the rules forbid editing SQL.

sources.note: modules/mysql/server.lua builds its query table from {user_table}/{vehicle_table} gsub placeholders; the qbx resolution (players/citizenid, player_vehicles/id) was substituted and those rows are marked normalised. There is no top-level server.lua or init.lua in the current tree.
sql/community_mrpd.sql and sql/default.sql are door-data seeds, not schema; not harvested.
server/vehicle-persistence.lua contains no SQL at all - it persists through qbx_vehicles exports. server/player.lua also contains no SQL; all of it lives in server/storage/players.lua.
Harvested because qbx_core delegates all vehicle persistence here.
No .sql file; the resource relies on qbx_vehicles' schema.
Creates its own tables at runtime; richest source of date/interval and aggregate constructs.
esx-framework/esx_legacy 404s - the repository was renamed/superseded by esx-framework/esx_core, which is what was harvested.
server.lua is legacy MySQL.Async/exports.oxmysql style but was not reachable within the fetch budget; only the DDL was harvested.
